propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate built the promotional-uplift features for the weekly SKU-level forecasting model and maintained them as a scheduled Airflow pipeline.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the work and the lead data scientist confirmed it in writing.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate ran the monthly backtests of the forecasting model and reported the results to the lead data scientist, who decided which model changes went forward.
propositions.rationale: The resume places the change decisions with the lead data scientist and the reference confirms the backtests.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate owned the SKU-level forecasting model from prototype to business sign-off and decided its model changes.
propositions.rationale: Ownership appears only as praise quoted on a self-prepared slide, which is a subjective remark and not a record of decisions; the resume states that the lead data scientist decided the model changes.

expectedGap: The sources document feature, backtest and reporting work on the model; deciding model changes and leading the business sign-off are not documented.
expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the features, pipeline, backtests, accuracy reviews and model-card sections as stated; the quoted praise on the slide does not show who decided model changes.
permittedFollowUpTargets: Ask which model changes or sign-off steps the candidate decided personally, and what the lead data scientist decided.
